f8e29347aa6b5554c832b1aea18ef044a05b9ca9.summary: eSentire's Threat Response Unit reports an intrusion that began with a fake snipping-tool download page and a Microsoft-signed store installer. That installer led to 'Setup Assistant', an obfuscated Electron app in the Microsoft Store, which acted as a backdoor executing C2-supplied PowerShell and JavaScript. It then deployed Vinci RAT, a PowerShell-based RAT with remote and reverse shell access, file staging, and several execution methods. Persistence used a scheduled task, and an AMSI bypass was observed. The report says Microsoft found the app did not violate its terms despite the TRU…

AlphV says an intrusion via one of its hosting providers exposed decryption keys for about 400 companies, and it announces removing its rules against targeting hospitals and nuclear power plants, raising the affiliate rate to 90%, and harsher treatment of victims. These are AlphV's own claims, reproduced by the outlet and not independently confirmed in the text.

f8b56cdf8ac2641660351f4a0c587ecaa361564c.summary: SentinelOne research on two ransomware-as-a-service brands, HellCat and Morpheus. Their payloads are almost identical, and the report believes one affiliate uploaded samples for both in late December 2024. The ransom notes follow the same template as those of Underground Team, but the report finds insufficient evidence of a shared codebase or partnership between the groups and suggests a shared builder may be in use. The LockBit group took credit and set a ransom deadline of February 28. The agency said transit operations were not affected, was still investigating what sensitive data was accessed, and planned to notify customers if their information was stolen. The report also lists other transit ransomware incidents and a 2023 attack on New York City's transit authority by a group based in…
